finding: The live range is about right, if slightly generous at the top. Our built totals for a belt kit with water pump (parts + hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks) are: economy 2005 Civic 1.7L $451-$798; midsize 2019 Odyssey 3.5L V6 $635-$1,136; truck 2006 Tundra 4.7L V8 $668-$1,223; luxury 2008 Audi A4 2.0T FSI $891-$1,207. That gives an overall span of about $450-$1,225 against the live $500-$1,475. The bottom is fine: only a four-cylinder economy engine with an aftermarket kit lands near $500, and KBB's general range starts at $409. The top is higher than anything we can build at $160/hr, but the main benchmarks top out at $1,302-$1,338 and KBB shows dealer quotes to about $1,500, which reflects dealer labor rates above $160/hr and genuine parts, so keeping the top near $1,475 is defensible. Our V6/V8 totals sit a little below the benchmark averages (about $900-$1,300) mostly because the labor times we could source are tight. How solid each labor time is: the midsize low end (3.1 hours) is Honda's own warranty flat-rate time for the example vehicle, the 2019 Odyssey, and the Acura version of the same recall prints 2.9-3.2 hours for the same engine family; it is a warranty time for the belt alone, so a shop adding the water pump will bill more, and the 4.3-hour high end is only a forum post about an older Honda/Acura V6. The truck low end (3.7 hours) is a Gates installation-sheet time for the same 4.7L V8 in a 4Runner, not the Tundra, and does not say it includes the water pump; the 4-5 hour figure is one independent shop's statement about the engine. The economy time is a single forum answer from a mechanic about a 2002 Civic 1.7L (2.7 hours plus about an hour for the pump), not a published labor guide. The luxury time (5.4 hours) is one named mechanic's figure for the 2008 Audi A4, so that range is a single value. Confidence stays low because the economy class rests on a forum answer alone and no manufacturer-stated time was found for the Civic, Tundra or Audi. Every class here includes the water pump; a belt-only job is cheaper in parts (for example $125 vs $127-$206 on the Civic, $104-$131 vs $243-$343 on the Audi) and roughly an hour less labor on the Civic. Parts gaps: no genuine Honda or Audi kit list price was found, so the Honda high ends are the list price of an aftermarket or original-supplier kit (on the Odyssey the genuine belt and tensioner alone list at $182.40 and $309.15); the Audi parts come from one confirmed retailer.
extras: Quotes often add: the water pump if it was not in the base quote; coolant and thermostat; accessory/serpentine drive belt; cam and crank seals; valve cover gasket; hydraulic tensioner and idler pulleys if the base quote was belt only; spark plugs or valve adjustment bundled as a major service on Honda V6s; one-time-use crank and engine-mount bolts on Audi/VW; shop supplies, coolant disposal fee and sales tax. If the old belt has already broken on an interference engine, expect a separate diagnosis charge and possible valve damage that this price does not cover.
